attributes.probed_form: VERDICT: NOT a label discrepancy and NOT a metric artefact. The two undefined externals name DIFFERENT data, and our source was reading the wrong one. Evidence, all from the current tree: config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt defines `lbl_80344408 = .sbss:0x80344408; type:object size:0x4 align:4 data:float` and `lbl_80344530 = .sbss:0x80344530; type:object size:0x4 align:4 data:float` -- two distinct 4-byte .sbss floats 0x128 apart, both already declared and used independently throughout camera.c (lbl_80344530 at 20+ sites, lbl_80344408 at 12+), and used as two DIFFERENT quantities in combat.c as well (lbl_80344530 is written as the target pitch, lbl_80344408 is read as the pitch it is compared against). The target's own three-instruction sequence settles the semantics: at +0x240 `lfs f0,lbl_80344530`; +0x244 `stfs f0,lbl_80344408`; +0x248 `lfs f0,lbl_80344408` -- it stores through to lbl_80344408 and then RELOADS FROM lbl_80344408, whereas our source re-read the source global instead. Cure, one word in src/game/world/camera.c: `cam0->pyr[0] = *(volatile f32*)&lbl_80344530;` -> `cam0->pyr[0] = *(volatile f32*)&lbl_80344408;` (the preceding line `*(volatile f32*)&lbl_80344408 = *(volatile f32*)&lbl_80344530;` is unchanged). Runtime behaviour is unaffected because the store immediately precedes the load, which is exactly why nothing caught it; the SYMBOL was nevertheless wrong. WHY objdiff AND fndiff BOTH read 100%/real 0 here, resolving the original disagreement: the lfs word is byte-identical on both sides (c0000000) since an EMB_SDA21 load encodes displacement zero and lets the relocation supply it, so a text comparison cannot see the difference at all -- and camera_mode_level is webfrank-PINNED, so fndiff scores the postprocessed object and reads real 0 by construction. The run-26 'fndiff OPERAND_DIFF 2 vs objdiff 100%' framing was therefore comparing two views that could BOTH only ever have been blind to the actual defect.
attributes.residual: The +0x248 row is closed. The relocation-symbol comparison that found it leaves ELEVEN further rows in camera_mode_level, all now classified. FOUR are REL24 callee names lacking the split's address suffix (get_attn_pos vs get_attn_pos_8002C9A8, calc_cam_pyr, get_cam_wpos, StandardCamera x3, ProcCamera) -- naming convention, not defects. SEVEN are MWCC anonymous pool labels where the target has named ones: @6 -> lbl_80345F58 at +0x4d0 and +0x620, @7 -> lbl_80345F60 at +0x4ec, +0x508, +0x63c, +0x658, @8 -> lbl_80345F68 at +0x4f8 and +0x648; debug_camera_pos adds @520 -> lbl_80345F50 at +0x13c, +0x184, +0x20c and @16 -> lbl_80345EB0 at +0x474. These are the SAME defect class this run fixed in CameraSupervisor and are a measured, ready-to-execute follow-up for game/world/camera: all three doubles are already declared as named externs in the sibling TU combat.c, so the conversion is mechanical. It was NOT executed here, deliberately: removing anonymous pool entries renumbers the object's symbol table and therefore invalidates the relocation hashes of ALL FOUR of this TU's pinned rules, including the debug_camera_pos rule banked THIS SESSION, so it must be done as its own gated stage with every pin re-derived (the procedure and the tooling are proven -- see claim.law.WF_a-pool-fix-renumbers-relocation-hashes-not-body-hashes.20260901.v1). Not attempting it inside this session protected a fresh exact.
